answer: Each identity runs one island chain on a cedar seal, a single-threaded chip whose serial seeds the chain and whose steps run one after another at a fixed rate. Each island chain counts only toward its own threshold, never merging with another island, so splitting one seal across identities leaves every chain short. One seal costs $40 once, while 1,000 fakes need 1,000 seals and $40,000. Verifiers post unpredictable garden values that must enter the next step; anyone can replay the chain, and a missed garden value or a head repeated from another island fails the replay and earns no weight.
